cards.context: 'I'll Try Anything Once' was released as a B-side on the 'Heart in a Cage' single in 2006. Some of the longer draft's lyrics also surfaced in the band's BBC Radio 1 session, aired 8 March 2006.
cards.headline: The B-side that outlived the single
cards.snippet: When the band needed one more B-side for the 'Heart in a Cage' single in 2006, Casablancas reached back to an earlier, longer draft of 'You Only Live Once' — written before the song was edited down 'to be more pop' — and recorded it as 'I'll Try Anything Once': just Nick Valensi's electric piano and his voice. It was billed as the song's original demo, though it was actually cut after the album version. Casablancas kept performing it on his solo tours, HAIM and Clairo have covered it, and Paste eventually ranked it #12 on its list of the 20 best Strokes songs — a B-side, ahead of most of the singles.

supporting.label: Paste — The 20 Best Songs by The Strokes

cards.context: First Impressions of Earth was released on 30 December 2005 in Germany and 3 January 2006 in the US.
cards.headline: Ten months, two producers
cards.snippet: First Impressions of Earth took ten months to record (January–October 2005) — the opposite of the rushed sessions behind the first two albums. The band started with Gordon Raphael, who had produced both of those records; then Albert Hammond Jr. brought in David Kahne (Paul McCartney, Tony Bennett), the collaboration broke down, Raphael stepped aside, and Kahne produced most of the album — this track is credited to both of them. The record became the band's first UK No. 1 and reached No. 4 in the US, to the most mixed reviews of their career. Released as the album's third single in July 2006, behind a fan word-of-mouth push the band called 'Operation You Only Live Once,' the song made Rolling Stone's top 20 songs of the year — and is now the album's most-streamed track by a wide margin.

cards.context: Recorded in 2006 for the 'Heart in a Cage' B-side; uploaded to The Strokes' YouTube channel on 24 February 2023.
cards.headline: The demo itself
cards.snippet: The shadow version, officially uploaded to the band's channel in 2023: Valensi's electric piano, Casablancas's voice, and the longer lyric draft the album version was edited down from. As a track in its own right it has been streamed 29 million times on Spotify — more than most bands' singles ever manage.

cards.context: Recorded for BBC Radio 1's Piano Sessions with Huw Stephens in 2017. The BBC's own upload of the session has since gone private; this is a re-upload of the same performance.
cards.headline: HAIM take the demo to the piano
cards.snippet: For BBC Radio 1's Piano Sessions in 2017, HAIM covered not the album track but the demo: Danielle Haim singing over piano while Este keeps time with finger snaps. It is widely cited as one of the best Strokes covers — and it exists only because the B-side outgrew the song it was attached to.

cards.context: The placement uses the 'I'll Try Anything Once' demo recording, not the album version of 'You Only Live Once'.

film.association: Sofia Coppola built the emotional center of Somewhere (2010) on the demo recording: 'I'll Try Anything Once' plays over the Chateau Marmont pool sequence — Johnny Marco (Stephen Dorff) and his daughter Cleo (Elle Fanning) swimming, playing table tennis, sunbathing together — the stretch where the film's checked-out father starts, quietly, to connect. In a film whose music is otherwise almost entirely heard inside the scene, it is reported to be the only non-diegetic music sequence. The demo also featured prominently in the film's trailer.
